svg.text: Multi-Vendor Integration Pattern — The Shape, and Where It Drifts
InstantMudra Enterprises Admin Portal
The intended 3-layer pattern — worked example: AEPS merchant onboarding
AepsVendorService (interface)
one impl per vendor, e.g.
FingPayAepsServiceImpl
AepsVendorFactory
exact key match, falls back to
substring key.contains(code)
AepsOrchestrator
routing → credentials → vendor bean → call
— but only 82 lines, ONE method: registerMerchant()
VendorRouting — config model (per sub-product)
routingPriority1 / 2 / 3 (Vendors FK) — CommonMethods.getVendors() returns the first ACTIVE priority slot, in order
Also stores volume1-3 / value1-3 / volumeNumberOfTxn / volumeValueOfTxn / valueValueNumberOfTxn / valueValueOfTxn —
columns shaped for percentage/threshold-based traffic splitting across vendors
⚠ getVendors() never reads any of the volume/value columns — only simple priority failover is actually implemented
AEPS / DMT / Recharge / Payout factories
fallback match: registeredKey.contains(requestedCode)
— unordered HashMap iteration if multiple keys match
PaymentGatewayInitiatorFactory
fallback match: first whitespace-separated word only
— a completely different, independently-invented strategy
Where the pattern drifts — three different shapes, all verified by line count
AEPS — total bypass
AepsOrchestrator: 82 lines, one method — merchant onboarding only.
InstantpayAepsTransactionServiceImpl: 1,171 lines — balance inquiry, cash withdrawal, mini-statement,
ALL of it — resolves its own vendor routing independently, never calls AepsVendorFactory or AepsOrchestrator.
14× the size of the "official" orchestrator, and it's the code path actually doing the work.
DMT — parallel duplication
DmtOrchestrator: 2,207 lines — large, and genuinely the active, used orchestration path.
RemitterServiceImpl (936 lines) + DmtBeneficiaryServiceImpl (829 lines) — older, Paysprint-hardcoded
implementations that run alongside the orchestrator, not replaced by it.
Two live code paths for the same domain — which one actually handles a given request depends on which controller/
endpoint was called, not on any single source of truth.
BBPS — hybrid: looks up config, then ignores it
BBPSServiceImpl (759 lines) DOES query VendorRoutingRepository.findBySubProductId() — so it looks like
config-driven routing — but then hardcodes the literal string "A2Z" into the transaction record and description
regardless of what the routing actually resolved to. RechargeVendorFactory is never called from this file.
Non-functional stub vendors — not even registered as Spring beans
AirtelAepsServiceImpl, A2ZRechargeServiceImpl, FingpayDmtServiceImpl — each implements its vendor interface but
carries no @Service / @Component annotation, so Spring never instantiates them — they're absent from the factory's
constructor-injected List<VendorService> entirely, on top of every method already returning null/empty. Routing to
"airtel" / "a2z" / "fingpay" fails at the factory lookup, before any stub method would even run.
Standard / as-designed
Correctly-routed, factory/orchestrator path
Flagged drift / dead config
Severe drift — pattern totally bypassed
